name: Amortization Schedule to Actuarial APR Check
outcome: Three-step chain. Step 1 rebuilds the amortization schedule from loan amount, note rate, and term, for level-payment, ARM, interest-only, balloon, and temporary-buydown structures, and for a payment derived from the note rate. Step 2 computes the actuarial annual percentage rate and finance charge from that schedule under 12 CFR 1026 Appendix J. Step 3 is the receipt step only. Step 1 matters for non-level schedules, where the payment stream is irregular and must be built before any rate is solved; for a level-payment loan, step 2 alone suffices, since its advances and payments are already a regular stream. This chain makes NO disclosed-APR comparison and NO section 1026.22(a) tolerance claim: step 2 emits no tolerance, and art-217-trid-apr-accuracy, which carries tolerance, is not in this chain. The finance charge equals total interest only when the schedule fully amortizes, with ending balance zero; for a balloon schedule the finance charge differs by the ending balance. The actuarial APR is a Regulation Z computation, not a GAAP ASC 470 effective interest rate, and fees and costs enter it only if they are in the payment stream. Art-332 has no fee input: its advances are one amount equal to the full loan amount, so the amount financed in step 2 is the full loan amount. Prepaid finance charges, including points and origination fees, are not modelled. The APR from this chain is therefore not the Regulation Z disclosed APR when such fees exist; for an ordinary loan it is close to the note rate. Compare this APR to a disclosed APR only for fee-free loans. Federal math only; not legal advice and not tax or accounting advice.
